- 🔊 **Recording sound cues (opt-in)** - enable in Settings to hear a short high tone when dictation starts and a low tone when it stops - eyes-free confirmation and a pacing cue so you don't clip the start of your speech. Tones are generated in memory and played non-blocking; dictation is never delayed or broken if audio playback fails. (requested by @MaxiKingXXL)

- 🛡️ **Hold-mode recording safety cap** - if a key-release event is ever lost, hold-to-record could previously leave the microphone recording indefinitely. `MAX_RECORD_SECONDS` now caps *both* recording modes; when the cap is hit in hold mode the mic stops and the audio is discarded (never pasted), and the shared recorder now tracks a single session owner so audio can't leak from one mode into another. (root-caused by @MaxiKingXXL)

- 🤖 **OpenAI-compatible providers** - the assistant now works with llama.cpp, LM Studio and any OpenAI-compatible local server, not just Ollama. Pick the provider in Settings; models are discovered automatically via `/v1/models`, and each provider keeps its own URL and model settings. (thanks @aladin7)

- 🖼️ **Clipboard keeps your images and files** - dictating no longer destroys non-text clipboard content: screenshots, copied files and other formats are preserved and restored after the paste. If you copy something new while WritHer is pasting, your fresh copy wins. Restore delay is configurable via `CLIPBOARD_RESTORE_DELAY`. (thanks @aladin7)

When opted in, drt sends one `sync_completed` event per sync. The **only `properties`** we collect are these 9 fields: `drt_version`, `python_version`, `os`, `source_type`, `destination_type`, `sync_mode`, `rows_synced`, `duration_seconds`, `status`. The wire envelope additionally carries `event`, `distinct_id` (a per-machine random UUID at `~/.drt/.anonymous_id`), `timestamp`, and `api_key`. Sync names, model SQL, destination URLs, credentials, and project paths are **never** transmitted — the allow-list is enforced at the function-signature level in `drt/telemetry.py`. By default events go to **PostHog Cloud (EU region)**; override with `DRT_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT` and `DRT_TELEMETRY_API_KEY` for self-hosted PostHog or a custom collector.
> Note: drt itself never transmits your IP, but the receiving PostHog backend records the TCP source IP as `$ip`. See docs/telemetry.md for details and how to disable / substitute the backend.

Modern data sources offer `OceanBaseDataSourceBuilder.UseClientCertificate(...)`. Build captures an owned copy even with pooling disabled, so the original can be disposed after Build succeeds. Source connections inherit fixed configuration. Certificate rotation uses a new data source; dispose the old source and close its borrowed connections when retiring that identity. Pooled borrow does not repeat TLS validation. See the client certificate contract for ownership and rotation limits.

For enterprise trust or certificate pinning, set `OceanBaseConnection.RemoteCertificateValidationCallback` before Open, or use `OceanBaseDataSourceBuilder.UseRemoteCertificateValidationCallback(...)`. This requires `TLS Mode=VerifyFull`. A callback replaces the platform validation decision and must handle certificate, chain, hostname and revocation errors; null retains platform validation. Ordinary pools isolate callback instances by reference. Validation runs at physical TLS establishment, not at each pooled borrow; rebuild/dispose the data source when retiring a trust policy. See the TLS API contract.

- Text multi-statements are opt-in with `Allow Multi Statements=true`. Oracle named and MySQL positional inputs support numbers, strings, binary, JSON (MySQL), NChar/NVarchar2 (Oracle) and NULL, plus MySQL DATE/DATETIME/TIMESTAMP/TIME and Oracle DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE/TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE/INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH/INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND. Oracle national inputs use ASCII Unicode literals, preserving characters outside the client charset; national result decoding requires fresh trusted state and uses the supported explicit encoding mappings. MySQL strings tolerate SQL_MODE changes but require stable parsing character sets. Binary Input streams use bounded client-literal encoding; MySQL scalar Output/InputOutput/ReturnValue positions use private user variables, with atomic publication after the script and a hidden output SELECT complete; reader close drains the active script. Script or output-query errors preserve prior parameter values but do not undo successful SQL. Stream/locator/complex outputs, Oracle script outputs, Prepare and server cursors remain unsupported. Oracle named complex input support is limited to the documented D-02d1 through D-02d3 and D-04f subsets. See compatibility for limits.
- MySQL stored procedures support binary InputOutput streams through prepared SET/CALL, with caller-owned sources and outputs published after complete results. See INOUT stream evidence.
- Opt-in client prepare fallback accepts MySQL BIT/YEAR inputs using exact numeric literals after a validated unsupported-Prepare response. See fallback evidence and deployment limits.

- Explicit MySQL JSON inputs also support that opt-in fallback, using fresh session charset/SQL_MODE facts and ordinary string literals. JSON syntax remains server-validated; see JSON fallback evidence.

- MySQL DATE/DATETIME/TIME inputs also support opt-in fallback, retaining exact input precision and current-session TIMESTAMP conversion. TIME cap fractions have server-specific binary/text differences; see temporal evidence and the completed/remaining checkpoint.

- Oracle binary InputOutput streams use the existing prepared piece upload and retain caller ownership. Outputs follow server metadata: the verified anonymous procedure wrapper returns RAW content as CHAR hex text. See Oracle INOUT stream evidence.

- Complex LOB inputs support named BLOB bytes/CLOB text and anonymous BLOB/CLOB arrays of session-bound locator handles. Single-statement Oracle Text/StoredProcedure named locator inputs use validated constructors with hidden root LOB binds; independent scalar and specified resource outputs, batch input-only subsets, and specified mixed batch routine-barrier output combinations are supported. Complex locator InputOutput and multi-statement expansion remain unsupported; see the complex type input contract.

- CLOB locator parameters convert inline content in a sending copy for configured client charsets (V1; V2 on authenticated OceanBase4.4.1+). Original handles and UTF-8 readers retain their bytes; see the charset contract.

- MySQL ARRAY values use the existing String parameter/result path. Current direct acceptance covers INT nesting and single-level TINYINT/SMALLINT/BIGINT/FLOAT/DOUBLE/VARCHAR arrays. Results preserve the server representation: FLOAT array text may round values, and VARCHAR array text may contain raw control characters and incomplete JSON escaping. Do not assume lossless text rebinding or JSON parsing; see compatibility.

- Named Oracle OBJECT/collection values support exact INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH and DAY TO SECOND members in binary inputs/results and PL OUT/INOUT, including named client-constructor inputs. Use the existing interval provider values. Named OBJECT and nested OBJECT text results also decode exact INTERVAL members from the preloaded declaration (D-04f3; Oracle 4.4.2.2 direct, 24/24). Unknown declarations or malformed values are rejected; collection and other unsupported complex text shapes retain their guards. Canonical anonymous INTERVAL factories also support the verified ExecuteArray DML input/RETURNING subset (D-04f1); current PL outputs with unknown precision are rejected. Anonymous INTERVAL result descriptors now reuse the embedded-precision codec; explicitly declared precision-9 PL local collection OUT has initial direct evidence (D-04f2), but extended live acceptance is incomplete after endpoint handshake failures. Ordinary anonymous 0x17 binding and dedicated multi-send acceptance remain open. See D-04f in the roadmap.

- `GetSchema` exposes 20 Oracle-mode / 18 MySQL-mode collections, including views, indexes, keys/constraints, foreign keys, sequences and users; Oracle also provides named types and synonyms. `Restrictions` describes exact bound filters; static `DataTypes` reports CLR/provider mappings and conditional codec support. See the Schema contract for permissions and mode limits; real directory/OBProxy validation remains open.

- `OceanBaseParameter.DecimalScale` declares signed decimal scale, including Oracle NUMBER negative scales. Values requiring rounding are rejected; MySQL retains its narrower limits. See the parameter contract for precedence and mode bounds. Real-server declared-scale validation remains open.

- `CredentialProvider` and modern builder `UseCredentialProvider` obtain one immutable credential per logical Open, including pool reuse. Higher versions retire old sessions without interrupting active borrowers; expiry, cancellation and refresh failures fail closed. Providers own caching/refresh and remain caller-owned. See the credential contract.

- `Pooling=true` reuses authenticated physical sessions, validates reused sessions, resets them before return, and supports `Min Pool Size`, `Max Pool Size`, `Pool Wait Timeout`, `Connection Idle Lifetime` and `Connection Lifetime`; `Min Pool Size` prewarms physical sessions before a borrow and rolls back sessions still idle after a failed warmup, preserving sessions already borrowed by concurrent Opens. Recognized user session-state and temporary-object statements discard the physical session instead of returning it to the pool. Opening inside an ambient `TransactionScope` enlists one local transaction through the coordinator single-resource slot. A second database resource and distributed promotion are rejected. Lost COMMIT responses report InDoubt; automatic `OpenAsync` initialization observes the opening cancellation token and discards an interrupted session. Cancelling that token after Open completes does not cancel the transaction. See the ambient contract.

- `OceanBaseConnection.ClearPool(connection)` closes idle sessions for that identity and discards borrowed sessions when returned. `ClearAllPools()` clears ordinary registry pools; private data sources use `source.Clear()` or `ClearPool` with one of their connections. Active commands continue, and new Opens remain available. See the pool clearing contract.

- Every connection confirms `ob_version()` and the tenant compatibility mode; MySQL-mode opens also require `@@autocommit` enabled, rejecting sessions whose implicit transactions this provider could not commit. Oracle opens explicitly confirm `set autocommit = 1`; pool return repeats it after successful reset, discarding the session on failure. See the Oracle baseline contract. Recognized version formats are accepted; versions beyond the recorded deployment and OBProxy still need real-server validation.
